subject: Endurance & Surge Profile — evidence for graceful degradation and scaling
messages:

Subject: RFP follow-up: endurance & surge evidence request

Jordan —

Thanks for the materials you sent earlier in the packet. For our procurement and SRE review we need more granular evidence around two areas before we can advance:

1) An endurance run that demonstrates steady-state behavior over long windows (we typically ask for 6–12 hours) with token/cost breakdowns and memory/KV-cache stability.
2) A short-duration surge test that simulates 2x–5x concurrent QPS for 10–30 minutes and shows how the system degrades (latency percentiles, tail behavior, and exact fallback steps).

Specifically please provide:
- The complete run artifacts (CSV + raw logs) for an 8-hour run if available.
- A short narrative explaining the graceful degradation path (which model variants, routing policies, and any blocking throttles are involved).
- Any playbook you use for repeatable execution (commands, workloads, traffic mix).

We aim to close the performance section of the RFP by Monday the 8th. Can you confirm whether you can deliver the artifacts and a short summary by EOD Monday?

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Thompson
SRE Lead, Glacial Systems

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can provide the 8-hour endurance artifact and a 15–30 minute surge run demonstrating controlled 2x and 4x bursts. Draft plan (high level):

- Deliverables by EOD Monday (8th): endurance_run_results.csv, surge_run_logs.tar.gz, and a 2-page playbook (graceful_degradation_playbook.pdf).
- Methodology summary included in the attached notes: steady-state warmup (1 hour at baseline QPS), KV prefix-cache warmup script, and diurnal noise injection to simulate real traffic.
- Graceful degradation path: automatic routing to quantized model variant (fp16->int8 quantized profile), dropping batch-size for latency SLOs, and ephemeral throttling to protected tenant pools. We will supply measured p50/p95/p99 and tail latency decomposition (dispatcher, runtime, kernel stalls).

I’m looping in Marissa and Monica who ran the experiments. If you prefer a short screen-share to walk through the artifacts, we can offer a 30-minute slot on Monday morning.

-Jordan

Subject: Fwd: Re: RFP follow-up: endurance & surge evidence request

Aisha —

Attached are the artifacts and a concise methodology. Key highlights up front:

- Endurance run: 8h steady-state at baseline QPS=150 (mixed prompt lengths; avg token/sec 42). Warmup: 1h synthetic ramp + prefix-cache prefetching. Artifacts: endurance_run_results.csv (token-level timestamps, per-request latencies, model-variant flag), raw runtime traces in surge_run_logs.tar.gz.
- Surge window: two controlled bursts — 2x baseline for 15m and 4x baseline for 10m. During the 4x burst we observe: p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 210ms, p99 ~ 720ms for the primary model; automatic fallback to quantized-compact reduces p99 to ~320ms with slightly higher perplexity on a held-out prompt set.
- Graceful degradation steps (order observed in telemetry):
  1) Per-request routing to reserved-capacity replicas (latency neutral),
  2) If those saturate, dynamic routing to quantized variants (int8) with KV-cache translation (keeps prefix cache hits for top N prefixes),
  3) If still saturated, reject with soft-429 + recommended retry-after header (exponential backoff policy in SDKs),
  4) Fallback to read-only cached responses for idempotent prompt classes when appropriate.
- Deterministic reproducibility: we publish the run harness (traffic profile JSON) and the docker test image used for the driver; link attached.

Methodology summary (concise):
- Hardware: 8x A100-80GB per cluster shard for the run (dedicated pool); driver machines on GCP n2-standard-16.
- Models: primary (redwood-large-fp16), fallback (redwood-large-int8-compact).
- Metrics captured: request-level timestamps, device-exclusive compute time, kernel stalls, queueing delay, per-replica concurrency, token-level cost.
- Analysis: we provide time-series and percentile decomposition (dispatcher vs runtime) and a small notebook to reproduce the fig.

I've attached: endurance_run_results.csv (summary + per-request lines), surge_run_logs.tar.gz (raw traces + driver logs), graceful_degradation_playbook.pdf (playbook + CLI commands), and a one-page CSV->notebook readme.

If helpful, we can include a short excerpt of the p99 latency waterfall and the exact CLI flags we ran in the harness. We are available Monday 10:00–11:00 PT to walk through the data.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Performance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: endurance_run_results.csv, surge_run_logs.tar.gz, graceful_degradation_playbook.pdf

Marissa/Jordan —

Received and this is exactly the level of evidence our SRE and procurement teams were asking for. A few quick clarifying questions before we mark the performance section as complete:

- Can you confirm whether the KV-cache translation preserved prefix-hit rates above 80% during the 4x burst? If not, can you share a brief table showing prefix-hit percentages by time window?
- For the soft-429 behavior, what client-side SDK versions are required to see the retry-after header behavior (we saw mention of SDKs but want exact versions).
- Any additional notes on variance across AZs — the run appears to be single-region. Do you have equivalent evidence for cross-AZ routing behavior?

If you can provide those three quick datapoints by EOD Wednesday, we will move to finalize the RFP and convert the LOI to an initial purchase order.

Best,
Tom Grant
Head of Infrastructure, Glacial Systems
